reasons: forecast_missing: the board registered questions to be answered BEFORE the line and the form carries no answer, or fewer answers than questions -- a forecast collected after the line is a rationalisation

answers.q1_what_did_you_play: I played Bag of Tricks first, taking the option to spend 3 Sparks and place 3 Bombs dealing 5. Then I played Mine Toss on Shrinker Beetle, placing one more Bomb dealing 5. Finally I played Spirited Away for 12 Block. This uses all 3 Energy and all 3 starting Sparks, places 4 Bombs total, and should deal 20 damage by the start of next turn while leaving me with 4 Sparks from the 4 Bomb detonations.
answers.q2_other_line_considered: I seriously considered playing Bag of Tricks for the 3-Bomb option, Mine Toss, Duck and Cover, and Run Away! for 9 Block instead of Spirited Away. I also considered a more defensive line such as Duck and Cover, Spirited Away, and Run Away! for 17 Block, but it gave up all Bomb damage and Spark generation.
answers.q3_what_it_gave_up: The chosen line gave up the maximum possible Block. With 3 Energy I could have played Duck and Cover, Spirited Away, and Run Away! for 17 Block, or at least kept more defensive flexibility. It also gave up the option to keep the 3 Sparks unspent by taking Bag of Tricks’ 1-Bomb option, which would have produced more Sparks but much less immediate damage.
answers.q4_different_intent: Yes. If the enemy had telegraphed a large Attack instead of a Debuff, I would have weighed the 17-Block line much more seriously, because the chosen line only guarantees 12 Block while spending all Energy on damage. A high-damage Attack intent could make the extra 5 Block from Duck and Cover and Run Away! more valuable than the extra Bomb damage.

survives_means: not yet falsified -- this funnel refuses turns and never rates them

targets.rule: a play that names a card whose effects aim at ONE enemy must carry that enemy's printed name in `target`; a card that aims at nobody must carry `target: null`
targets.derived_from: the card sheets (understudy/resource_order.SHEETS: the three character sheets, the three companion sheets and docs/prototype-surface.yaml), read through each effect's own `target:` key. The blind packet carries NO targeting field -- the wire's hand entry has none -- so the sheet is the derivation and this is the record of it
targets.repair: out of scope by M63: this refuses a form and never repairs one

closeness_quotability: the decision-closeness gap is a falsifier reading of the TURN and is quotable under R215 B's exception; it is never evidence that a decision is fun
guardrail: staged board: this hand and this board were set by hand through a dev door, so nothing measured here is comparable to any run, and nothing here is a claim about whether the turn is fun
